questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Half-life period of a radiactive substance is 10 min , then amount of substance decayed in 40 min will be
questions.solution:
Number of half-lives in 40 min
$n=\frac{40}{T_{1 / 2}}=\frac{40}{10}=4$
Amount of the substance remaining after $n$ half- lives
$N=N_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n=N_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^4=\frac{N_0}{16}$
where, $N_0$ is original amount of the substance.
Amount of the substance decayed in 40 min .
$N^{\prime}=N_0-N=N_0-\frac{N_0}{16}=\frac{15}{16} N_0=  \left(\frac{15}{16} \times100 \%\right)$ of $N_0=15 \times6.25 \%$ of $N_0=93.75 \%$ of $N_0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Nuclear reactor in which U-235 is used as fuel. Uses 2 kg of $\mathrm{U}-235$ in 30 days. Then, power output of the reactor will be (given energy released per fission $=185 \mathrm{MeV}$ )
questions.solution:
Number of atoms in 2 kg of uranium
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{6.02 \times 10^{23}}{235} \times 2000 \\ & =5.12 \times 10^{24}\end{aligned}$
Therefore, energy obtained from these atoms
$\begin{aligned} & =5.12 \times 10^{24} \times 185 \mathrm{MeV} \\ & =5.12 \times 10^{24} \times 185 \times 10^6 \mathrm{eV}\end{aligned}$
Energy obtained per second
$=\frac{5.12 \times 10^{24} \times 185 \times 10^6 \times 16 \times 10^{-19}}{30 \times 24 \times 60 \times 60}$
Solving the above expression
$\begin{aligned} & =58.47 \times 10^6 \mathrm{ W} \\ & \cong 58.5 \mathrm{MW}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $Order of magnitude of density of uranium nuclus is (m_p=1.6 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{ kg}$ )
questions.solution:
Radius of a nucleus is given by
$\begin{aligned}
R & =R_0 A^{1 / 3}\left(\text{ where, } R_0=1.25 \times 10^{-15} \mathrm{ m}\right) \\
& =1.25 \times 10^{-15} A^{1 / 3} \mathrm{ m}
\end{aligned}$
Here, A$ is the mass number and mass of the uranium nucleus will be
\begin{aligned} m & \approx A m_p, m_p=\text{ mass of proton } \\ & =A\left(1.67 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{ kg}\right)\end{aligned}\therefore \quad$ Density $=\frac{\text{ Mass }}{\text{ Volume }}=\frac{m}{\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3}=\frac{A\left(1.67 \times 10^{-27}\right)}{A \times \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times\left(1.25 \times 10^{-15}\right)^3}\Rightarrow \quad \rho=2 \times 10^{17} \mathrm{ kg} / \mathrm{m}^3\therefore$ order is $10^{17}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When ${ }_{90} \mathrm{Th}^{228}$ transforms to ${ }_{83} \mathrm{Bi}^{212}$, then the number to the emitted $\alpha$ and $\beta$-particles is, respectively
questions.solution:
$Z=90 \mathrm{Th}^{A=228} \longrightarrow Z^{\prime}=83 \mathrm{Bi}^{A^{\prime}=212}$
Number of $\alpha$-particles emitted $n_\alpha=\frac{A-A^{\prime}}{4}=\frac{228-212}{4}=4$
Number of $\beta$-particles emitted $n_\beta=2 n_\alpha-Z+Z^{\prime}=2 \times 4-90+83=1.$

questions.q: As a result of radioactive decay ${ }_{92} \mathrmU^{238}$ is converted into ${ }_{91} \mathrm{ Pa}^{234}$. The particles emitted during this decay are
questions.solution:
Decrease in mass number $=238-234=4$ No. of $\alpha$-particles emitted $=\frac{4}{4}=1$
Decrease in atomic number due to emission of $1 \alpha$-particle is 2 , but now atomic number is 91.
Hence, number of $\beta$-particles = $91+2$ - 92 = 1.

$\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{t}{T}=$4 \quad$\left[\because$n=$\frac{t}{T}\right]\Rightarrow \quad$t=4 T=4 $\times$100 \mu $\mathrm{~s}\therefore \quad$t=400 \mu $\mathrm{~s}$

questions.q: Two $\mathrm{Cu}^{64}$ nuclei touch each other. The electrostatics repulsive energy of the system will be

Distance between two nuclei $(r)=2 R$
So, potential energy $U=\frac{k \cdot q^2}{r}=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times\left(1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 29\right)^2}{2 \times 4.8 \times 10^{-15} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}=126.15 \mathrm{MeV}$

questions.q: Decáy constant of radium is $\lambda$. By a suitable process its compound radium bromide is obtained. The decay constant of radium bromide will be
questions.solution: Many nuclei are radioactive. This means that they are unstable like radium and will eventually decay by emitting as particle transforming the nucleus into another nucleus. A chain of decays take place until a stable nucleus is reached. In the compound radium bromide, radium is radioactive while bromide is not, hence decay constant of compound is same as that of radium that is $\lambda$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The biological damage caused by 1 gray $\alpha$-radiation is compared with 1 gray $\gamma$-radiation in the same type of human tissue.
The damage caused by the $\gamma$-radiation is
options: more serious as compared to the damage caused by the $\alpha$-radiation.
less serious as compared to the damage caused by the $\alpha$-radiation
equally serious as the damage caused by the $\alpha$-radiation
incomparable with the damage caused by the $\alpha$-radiation, because $\gamma$-radiation are not particles.
questions.solution: The damage caused by the $\gamma$-radiation is less serious as compared to damage caused by the $\alpha$-radiation. This is because $\alpha$-radiation is more dangerous than beta or gamma if ingested because its power to ionize or to disrupt, atoms is 20 times more than $\beta$ and $\gamma$. But if the source is outside the body or at a distance gamma radiation is much dangerous because it could penertrate thick walls of skin.
